applies.reason: Covering doctors could open the notes of any registered patient, not only patients they are caring for.
Opening charts outside a care relationship has no typed reason and no privacy officer review.
The cheapest region is overseas, so patient data would be stored outside the country.
It does not say whether the hosting supplier has signed a data processing agreement.
Full name and date of birth are confirmed before the chart is opened.
The latest growth chart figure may be older than thirty days.
It changes what prescribers see, and it does not say a clinical safety assessment will be done before release.
Results are released before the ordering clinician has reviewed them.
Charts are merged by one user with no second staff confirmation.
Names and addresses stay in the research data when it leaves the clinical system.
It does not say whether patients consented to the disclosure.
Consulting room desktops would stay open for a whole session instead of locking after five minutes idle.
It does not say whether identity is confirmed with a one-time code at the start of the call.
Interaction warnings could be switched off for later prescriptions.
Contact consent is bundled with consent to treatment.
Parents would see data on 16 and 17 year olds without the young person's agreement.
The allergy check can be skipped with no reason entered.
Originals are binned the same day instead of kept for three months, and no legibility check is stated.
A reason is typed before the chart opens, and the privacy officer reviews each case within five working days.
The SMS includes clinical content and is not limited to patients who chose detailed messages.
A reminder the day before is less than forty-eight hours ahead.
Repeats would run for two years, beyond the twelve-month review limit.
Prescriptions and referral letters must carry the legal name, not the preferred name.
Reporting on the next working day misses the four-hour limit, and the report goes to IT rather than the privacy officer.
A relative interprets a consent conversation instead of a qualified interpreter.
The original text, who made the correction and the reason are all kept.
It does not say whether the device is in the inventory, with owner and software version, before it is connected.
Five years is shorter than the required eight-year retention.
It does not say whether the memory stick is an encrypted drive issued by the IT service desk.
Reception would see diagnoses.
It changes the clinical screen, and it does not say a clinical safety assessment will be done before release.
Six weeks exceeds the thirty-day response limit.
The email carries clinical referral details without checking that the patient opted into detailed messages.
It does not say whether a copy of the emailed letter is kept on the chart.
Weekly submission misses the twenty-four-hour reporting limit.
It changes the prescribing screen, and it does not say a clinical safety assessment will be done before release.
The laptops have encrypted disks and can be wiped remotely.
